evidence.shows: The refresh condition is keys === null || keys.size === 0 || age >= ttlMs, and age is measured from fetchedAt.
On failure with a usable stale set, nothing is updated, so the next call fetches again.

title: During a JWKS outage every verification re-attempts the network fetch until the stale window ends. (raised by the question sets behaviour and contracts)
body: When a refresh fails but the old key set is still within maxStaleMs, getKey serves the old keys and does not update fetchedAt. The age therefore stays at or above ttlMs, and every later call to getKey runs refresh() again. Calls that overlap share one request, but calls that do not overlap each start a new fetch that can wait up to the 5 s timeout. For up to an hour of outage, each authenticated request can be delayed by that timeout and adds load to the failing Auth endpoint. The header comment says a short outage should not reject valid sessions, but it does not say that requests slow down.
recommendation: Record the time of the last failed attempt and skip refetching for a short backoff while the stale set is still usable.

After a successful confirm, the parent closes the dialog by setting `open` to false. The next open then shows the previous reason, and an `acknowledgement` checkbox that is already ticked. title: Choosing a link entry closes the menu without returning focus
body: The link entry's onClick only calls setOpen(false). The focused menuitem link is then unmounted, so focus falls to <body> unless the navigation lands somewhere that takes it. Action entries go through close(true) and return focus to the trigger. The design system's own Dialog and focusReturn modules guard against this kind of focus drop, so link entries are treated differently from action entries. No current caller passes a link entry (UserCard uses only text, action and separator entries), so it only shows up once one does.
recommendation: Use close(false) plus a focus move to the main region (MAIN_REGION_ID) for link entries, or call close(true) so focus returns to the trigger.

evidence.shows: The loop breaks on `value < 1024` before the value is rounded.
Values of 100 or more are rounded with `Math.round`, which can give 1024.
`Math.max(minutes, delta >= 0 ? 1 : 0)` forces `1 min` at zero and allows `0 min` in the past.

title: formatBytes shows 1024 KB near a unit boundary, and formatTimeRemaining gives odd output at zero (raised by the question sets behaviour and contracts and repeats)
body: For 1048575 bytes, `value` is 1023.999, which is below 1024, so the loop stops at `kb`. Then `Math.round` gives `1024`, so the result is `1024 KB` instead of `1 MB`. In `formatTimeRemaining`, a delta of exactly 0 or a few seconds ahead renders `1 min left`. A deadline passed by under a minute renders `passed 0 min ago`.
recommendation: Round first and then choose the unit. Give sub-minute deltas their own wording, such as `now`.

title: Claim Detail can show the previous claim's tasks while the new claim's tasks load
body: useApiQuery keeps `data` from an earlier request while the endpoint, user, data set and as-of date are unchanged, even when the request differs. Navigating from one claim to another (as the test does, CLM-101 to CLM-104) therefore leaves `detail.tasks.data` holding the previous claim's tasks until the new tasks request settles. The page guards the claim and facts by claim id, but never guards tasks. TasksCard then lists the other claim's tasks, with their audit trails, under the new claim's heading. If the new tasks request fails, the stale list still shows instead of the error state, because `tasks.data === undefined` is false.
recommendation: Filter the task items to `subject_id === claim.claim_id`, or treat the result as unavailable while `tasks.isFetching` is true or the settled request is for a different claim. A `key={claimId}` on the page body that remounts the query does not help here, because the data lives in the hook's scope; the filter is the simpler fix.

body: task_audit_entries is granted only select and insert, and the comment says the role can 'never change or remove' an entry. title: The what-if event is not always the latest event: a real event with a time on the as-of date sorts after it
body: The hypothetical event is dated with the bare as-of date, which `momentMs` reads as 00:00 on that day (src/contracts/time.ts:11). The event id '~what-if' only wins ties on the same instant (time.ts:16). The as-of view keeps every event dated on or before the as-of date, including one with a time such as `2026-10-21T10:00:00+02:00`. In that case the real event sorts after the what-if one. The engine then reads the real stage as the current one, so the preview shows the real stage instead of the chosen one. Stage clock start and SLA are also wrong, and the stage check can report a mismatch, because the record's stage was moved to the chosen stage. The comment on WHAT_IF_EVENT_ID and DD-60 claim the event 'is always the latest event' and 'wins a tie on the same day', which only holds when the real events on that day are date-only.
recommendation: Date the hypothetical event at the end of the as-of day, for example `${asOf}T23:59:59+02:00`, or after the latest event already on the claim. Keep `event_at` in the answer as the date. Add a test with a timed event on the as-of date.
